basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Sed et Loth qui erat cum Abram fuerunt greges ovium, et armenta, et tabernacula; nec'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Sed et Loth qui erat cum Abram fuerunt greges ovium, et armenta, et tabernacula; nec poterat eos capere terra ut habitarent simul: erat quippe substantia eorum multa, et non quibant habitare communiter: unde et facta est rixa inter pastores gregum Abram et Loth, et caetera quibus ex ordine replicatur quomodo Loth ab Abraham salva charitate discessit, malente illo fratrem charissimum et sanctissimum a se corporaliter separari, quam cum scandalo et jurgiis infirmorum secum teneri: quem tamen a se corpore separatum nequaquam ab intimo suae mentis amore separavit, sicut sequentia sacrae historiae manifestissime probant: ubi eum ab hostibus captum strenuissime cum suis omnibus salvavit, et merito quia nec ipse Loth opus virtutis ac fidei, quod cum fratre majore consueverat exercere, etiam separatim conversatus ulla in parte mutavit.
